src/battle/BattleScene.js.s:
The light fades...
but it has not gone out.

src/data/content/ch2.js.s: Merry's Acorn
A small acorn, warm as a held hand. "The key to my secret place."
Thorne's Writ
"The girl is to be detained and conveyed to the Cathedral of Dawn. Unharmed." Sealed in black wax.
MAG +4, RES +4, MP +10%. Inscribed inside: "Keep the light."
Pell's Horseshoe
LCK +10, DEF +4. The third horseshoe from over the Pell farmhouse door.
Cliff Kite
Rides the Gale like a thrown knife. Nests in the cliffs and resents everyone below them.
Rockshell
A crab that took one look at the Gale and grew a boulder on its back.
Spume Jelly
Sea-foam that learned to hold a grudge. Spits salt in your eyes.
The Lord-Commander's personal guard. Black trim, a sun with a closed eye, and orders they will not explain.
Mourning Moth
They drink tears. In the Whisperwold they never go thirsty.
Hollow Sapling
A young tree with a hollow where its heart should be. Something whispers in the hollow.
Lost Shade
It is saying something. It has been saying it for a hundred years. It no longer knows to whom.
The oldest tree in the Whisperwold. She gathered the voices of the dead into her hollow so that none of them would ever be forgotten — or ever be allowed to end.
Three generations of Pells built him. One sack of cheap purple stuffing woke him up.
Bandit Bruiser
Red Tam hires by the pound.
Tam's Mastiff
Answers to "Biscuit." Do not call it Biscuit.
Rubblekin
Quarry stone that soaked up the violet seam beneath it, and got up.
Bethan, the Crestless Sage
Mender, Arcanist, Ranger, Cantor, Pugilist. "Same old woman. Different tools."
"Stay... stay... STAY."
Her bark splits wide open. A hundred voices weep at once!
"Come back to me, little ones..."
The Hollow Mother draws every voice in the wold into her branches...
Old Strawman bursts into violet flame!
Old Strawman flaps its sleeves. Crows pour out of its coat!
Violet dust gathers in Old Strawman's stitched grin...
"SHOOOOOOO!"
Harbor town of the Gale Coast. Sailors, smugglers, and the Salt & Lantern.
An ancient forest where the trees speak with the voices of the dead.
A farming village of beehives and autumn fields. Home of the Crestless Sage.

src/data/content/ch3.js.s: A bronze bell-hammer worn smooth by forty years of noons. Its name, scratched on the handle, is GLORIA.
A loose page from the Chronicle of the Long Night. Someone has inked over certain words. Thoroughly.
A large ginger cat, currently being carried by Sable. He is tolerating this.
Immune to Sleep and Silence. Beeswax, forty years of bells, and a little spite.
DEF +5, RES +5, HP +5%. Sir Aldous Venn's ring. Too big for any finger but his.
RES +5, Afterglow gain +15%. A handbell from the first carillon of Aurenne. It rings true.
The great bell tolls through bone.
The Gloam pulls at the edges of you.
The rooks of St. Aurel's have heard the bells every hour of their lives. It has not improved their mood.
Carved to spit rainwater off the roofs. Something down in the drains taught it to spit other things.
Grew fat on what the city flushes away. Is not grateful.
It drinks until it is round, then keeps drinking out of habit.
Lives on the Choir's candle-ends. Its dust smells like a cathedral and puts you to sleep like a sermon.
All bone and appetite. It still wags, which is worse.
Aurenne's old city watch. Still guarding the gate. The gate is gone.
A candle lit for the dead, forty years ago. Nobody blew it out.
A Sister of Small Mercies. She sings the Dawnsong. Something is wrong with the way she sings it.
Mercy gave it a memory to hold. It dropped it.
Several people, once. Mercy's notes call it "an economy of scale."
Wooden rules, first to yield. Nobody has ever told a squire that wooden swords still hurt.
The bell-founders of old Aurenne were buried beside their furnace. One of them got up to finish a job.
The City of Bells. Seat of the Choir, home of the Grand Lantern.

src/data/content/ch4a.js.s: Singing Saltglass
Lift-glass from the Glass Caverns. It hums when you hold it to the sun — and when you hold it near the tuning forks.
Halvard's Score
The Dawnsong in Brother Halvard's cramped hand. One note is circled twice. Beside it: REFLECTION?
Bell Stair Key
An iron key, warm from Halvard's hand.
Sand Blast
Siren Song
Erupt
Song of Breaking
Avalanche
Hold the Line
Execution Sweep
Thorne's Verdict
Shield Wall
Dune Scorpion
The color of the dunes at noon. You find out it is there when it finds out you are.
Wyrmling
A sand wyrm hatchling: the length of a man and all appetite. Its mother is never far.
Sun Wisp
A shimmer of heat that decided to stay. Drinks fire. Fears the dark.
Bone Vulture
It is patient. In the Sunscar, patience always eats.
Takes your water first. Then your boots. Then, if you complain, you.
Raider Slinger
Throws sand, stones and insults, all with remarkable accuracy.
Mirage
It wears the shape of what you want most. Up close it is only heat and hunger.
Sandmaw
A sand wyrm in its prime: forty feet of hunger that swims the dunes like open sea.
Raider-king of the southern dunes. Laughs like a jackal. Fights like three of them.
Glassback
Its shell is saltglass. It chimes when it walks, which is the only mercy it offers.
Prism Bat
Wings thin enough to throw rainbows. It throws them in your eyes.
Saltglass Golem
The caverns grow them like geodes. Nobody knows what wakes them. Something does.
Glass Crawler
Spins its webs from molten sand. They set like glass, and so do you.
Brood Wyrm
The Queen's children. Half-grown and wholly furious.
The Sand Wyrm Queen
She has eaten caravans whole. Her scales are saltglass; her song is the sound of the desert breaking.
Frost Wolf
Hunts in the white. Its coat is snow; its breath is the cold that comes after.
Crag Harpy
They sing travelers to sleep in the snow. The snow does the rest.
Rime Elemental
A winter that learned to walk. It does not hate you. It only wishes you were still.
Snowdrift Ogre
Sleeps under the snow for months. Wakes up hungry and offended.
Whitefang
Old as the monastery, the monks say. Every squire who ever kept the Vigil has heard it howl.
Icicle Bat
Hangs from the ceiling like an icicle. Falls like one too, but with teeth.
Gray cloaks over Dawnguard steel. They used to guard the dawn. Now they guard something else.
Vesper Arbalist
Crossbows wound with Choir prayers. The bolts still hurt.
They hum the same few notes over and over. After a while, you catch yourself humming them too.
Thorne's Guard
Garrick's chosen. They do not speak. They do not retreat.
Lord-Commander of the Dawnguard and the Hierophant's sword. Nobody has ever asked him to explain himself.
The sand ERUPTS beneath your feet!
Sandmaw shrieks. Something small and hungry answers from under the dunes!
Sandmaw dives beneath the sand... the dune begins to tremble.
"Ha! Lads — fresh meat, fresh water! GET IN HERE!"
Sarn kicks up a wall of sand!
The Queen bursts up through the glass floor!
The Queen SHRIEKS. The cavern walls crack — and the glass comes down like rain!
The Queen calls, and the walls answer with small hungry voices.
The Queen sinks into the sand. The glass floor starts to hum...
The Queen sings. Your armor sings back — and cracks.
The mountain answers Whitefang's howl!
Somewhere above, the pack answers.
Whitefang throws back its head and HOWLS. Snow shivers on the slopes above...
"Kneel, Kestrel."
"Judgement."
"Form up. Shields high. This will not take long."
Garrick wipes blood from his mouth and laughs. "Good. GOOD. Again."
"Enough." Garrick plants his greatsword in the snow. "Guard! To me!"
"Still shaking, Kestrel? Aldous would be so proud."
A town of glass and wind around the blind Keeper's Lantern. The caravans gather here.
The snow monastery, where the oldest Dawnsong is carved in ice.
Ysmay's Water & Sundries

src/data/content/ch4b.js.s: Lanternmoss
Moss that grew where a shrine-lamp burned for two hundred years. Still faintly warm. Glows when crushed.
Weepcap Lily
A white bog-lily that has never seen the sun. It weeps a clear sap that smells of rain.
Rot-Gall
The black heart of Mawmire. The sickness, made solid. Ilse handles it with tongs.
Tarnished Ring
A plain copper wedding ring, found in the Drowned Chapel. Engraved: _T. — always the long way home._
Clover Crown
A crown of clover, pressed flat and brown forty years ago. Lysa Lorne made it for Elowen. Sable keeps it now.
Storm Core
A fist of saltglass that has swallowed a lightning strike. It buzzes against your teeth.
Aram's Logbook
A sky-pilot's waterlogged logbook, found in the Undercradle. The last page is addressed to someone called Kesi.
Osk's Reed Knot
Immune to Poison and Blind. RES +4. Mirefen reed and silver wire; smells of peat smoke.
Pilot's Goggles
Immune to Blind. SPD +4, evasion +4%. Aram's spare pair; the strap still smells of wind.
Black Bile
A flood of rot-water.
Engulf
Root Quake
Thornstorm
Deep Drink
Lance of the Dawn
Stormfall
Downdraft
The Eye Opens
Bog Leech
Fat with other people's blood. Thin with its own patience.
Rot Toad
Mirefen children used to race the toads. Nobody races these.
Will-o'-Mire
Swamp-light. Follow it and you will find exactly what it wants you to find.
Marsh Crawler
Mud on the outside. Mud on the inside. A shell like a church door in between.
Rotcap
The Gloam-rot, grown a body. Its spores are the sickness in the village.
The Drowned
Mirefen buries its dead in the water. Since the light went out, the water has been giving them back.
Bog Lurker
The ferrymen call it "the log that moves." They do not call it anything to its face.
Rot Polyp
A bud of Mawmire. It wants to grow up to be just like its mother.
Mawmire
Where the Lantern's light used to touch the water, something grew in the dark to fill the space. It is mostly mouth.
Dawnguard Trooper
The Dawnguard swore to guard the light. These ones are guarding the Lord-Commander's temper.
Dawnguard Crossbow
Trained to hit a sparrow at sixty paces. Has never once been asked why.
Briarling
The Thornwood's youngest guardians. They have forgotten what they were guarding.
Mossback Boar
So old that moss grows on it. So angry that nothing else does.
Lost Lantern
A spark of the Thornwood's Lantern, left behind when its stone was taken. It is looking for the way home.
Bark Mantis
It prays. You do not want to know to what.
Gloam Moth
Drawn to light. There is none left in the Thornwood, so it has started making do with you.
Thornweaver
Weaves its webs from thorns. Silk has never occurred to it.
Rootlurker
A root that got tired of being underneath things.
Hollowbark
Warden of the Thornwood for six hundred years. Its Keeper's light went out, and it has been fighting the dark ever since — and everything else that moves.
Storm Cell
A thundercloud the size of a dog, and about as loyal.
Gale Harpy
Rides the Stormcrown's updrafts and screams at airships out of professional habit.
Crag Golem
Lightning hit this rock so many times it got up to complain.
Cloud Eel
It swims through cloud the way fish swim through water, and it is just as surprised to see you.
Storm Drake
Born in the Stormcrown, raised on lightning, and fond of airships the way cats are fond of birds.
Keel Sentinel
A watchman of brass and saltglass, set under Skyreach by its first Keepers. It has been watching for so long it forgot who it was watching for.
Dawnguard Lancer
Garrick's chosen. They polish their armor twice a day and their consciences never.
Captain of the Lord-Commander's Sunspears. Was in Bram's squire class. Has never let him forget it.
The Thunderhead
The Stormcrown's eye. For three hundred years Skyreach's Lantern held it down beneath the isle. The Lantern went dark, and the storm remembered it was alive.
Mawmire sinks into the black water. The bog itself seems to harden around it.
Mawmire's flank splits like rotten fruit. Something small and wet climbs out.
Mawmire drinks the bog. Its belly swells black. _Brace!_
The Warden does not see you. It sees only the dark it has been fighting for a year.
Hollowbark drives its roots into the earth. Briars claw up out of the soil!
Hollowbark drinks from the deep roots. Old sap closes its wounds.
Hollowbark's bark splits open, bristling with thorns as long as swords...
"Sunspears! Shields together!"
"Remember this, Kestrel? Stand still. You're good at that."
Corder levels his lance...
"Hold the line! For the Lord-Commander!"
The Thunderhead tears loose pieces of itself. They crackle into shape.
The clouds peel back. At the heart of the storm, an eye opens — and looks at you.
The wind falls silent. Your ears pop. The pressure is dropping...
Fern's Forage & Fletching
The Windward Exchange
A stilt village over the fens. Mother Osk keeps its Lantern — kept it.
The oldest forest in Solmere, and Rootholm at its edge. Elowen, the oldest Keeper, lives at its heart.
The rain-lashed foot of the Stormcrown, where the Halcyon waits on her cradle.
A floating isle of airship folk, riding the storm. Ardent Vasha keeps its Lantern.

src/data/content/ch5.js.s: Restores 1,200 HP and 60 MP to the party. Nana Brisa's brew for the night before every hard thing.
Ysolde's Bread
Restores 800 HP. Dense, a little burnt. Not as good as Nana's.
Duskwater Jelly
The tide pools of Lanternfall started glowing at night a week ago. This is why.
Gloamshell Crab
Its shell has gone the color of a bruise, and it rings like crystal when struck.
Drowned Fisher
Lanternfall has given men to the sea for four hundred years. The tide caves remember every one of them.
Tide Wraith
A cold shape that drifts above the pools, humming a lullaby nobody has sung in a hundred years.
Gloam Eel
The eels Ilse once complained about, changed. It is hard to say they are worse. They are certainly purpler.
Shardwing Bat
Its wings have grown crystal edges. It sounds like wind chimes when it dives at you.
Lord-Commander Thorne's own guard. They do not ask why. That is why he chose them.
Sunderhound
The first things to come through after the sky broke. Dogs made of dusk, with embers where their eyes should be.
Falling Ember
A fleck of the broken sun. It burns because it does not know how to do anything else.
The Tidemourner
Everything the sea ever took from Lanternfall, knotted together and wearing itself like a coat. It speaks in a voice you know.
Head of the Dawnguard and the Hierophant's sword. He has never once lost a duel, and has never once enjoyed winning one.
The Tidemourner brings the whole drowned sea down on you!
"...help us... it's so cold... help..." Hands claw up out of the water.
It calls again, in voices you almost know.
The Tidemourner draws in a long, wet, rattling breath...
It sings, in a man's voice, a song about a gull.
"VERDICT."
"Dawnguard! To me! Show these children what discipline looks like!"
Garrick lifts his greatsword high over his head. "Iron Verdict—"

src/data/content/ch6.js.s: Maela's Soup
Restores 700 HP and cures Poison and Burn. Ash-potato. It is always ash-potato.
Letter: "To Mama"
Water-stained. "To Mama, at Port Gale. From Jory." For the Lost Wall in Keelhaven.
Letter: "To Aldo"
Folded small, in a careful round hand. "To Aldo Brannock." For the Lost Wall in Keelhaven.
Letter: "To Teo"
Choir paper, sealed with candle-wax. "To my brother Teo, in Kiteholm." For the Lost Wall in Keelhaven.
Letter: "Dear Sun"
A child's writing, in crayon. "DEAR SUN." For the Lost Wall in Keelhaven.
The Sunward Atlas
Cassian's gift, swollen with damp. "For Wren, who asks the best questions. — C." You don't know why you kept it.
Choir Silk
White silk from the Gilded Psalm's banner, with a gold sunburst. For Pell's kite.
Glassback's Core
A fist-sized heart of living glass, still warm. Proof for Warden Hale's bounty.
The Lidless Eye
A cold violet orb. Do not look at it. It is looking at you. Proof for Warden Hale's bounty.
Fennick's Sailcloth Coat
Light armor. Max HP +8%. Three old sails and a Dawnguard cloak, terribly stitched. It keeps the ash off.
Ash Wraith
Ash that remembers being a person. It drifts toward warmth, and does not understand why the warm things scream.
Cinder Moth
Born in the embers that rained down after the sun broke. It is always flying toward the nearest fire, including yours.
Gloam Hound
The Gloam came up through the cracks in the world, and some of it came up hungry, and shaped like dogs.
Hollow Sailor
Still at its post on a ship that has no sea. It will defend the deck until the end of the world. Which is a problem, now.
Shard Golem
When the sea fell upward it left glass behind — miles of it — and some of the glass got up and walked.
Glasscrawler
It spins its webs between floating islands. Nobody knows what it catches up there. Nobody wants to.
Skybrine Eel
A sea eel, swimming through the air as if it never noticed the water leave. Perhaps it hasn't.
Sun-Ember Wisp
A fleck of the broken sun, still burning a year later. It is warm. Nothing else in the world is warm anymore.
Abyss Eye
The abyss under the islands is not empty. Sometimes it looks up.
Wreck Mimic
A sea-chest from some drowned rich man's cabin. It has learned that people will walk straight up to a sea-chest.
Old Fennick
Edrin Halloway's fishing partner. The light said Vanguard. He said "fish." The light didn't argue.
The Ashmaw
A hound of packed ash the size of a cart. It has been eating Fennick's chickens all winter.
Glassback
The biggest thing the glass ever made. It is so clear you can see the sky through it — bent, and broken, and beautiful.
The Lidless
It has no lid. It has never blinked. It has seen everything that has fallen past its perch for a year.
Brinefang, Unmoored
The serpent of the strait, still swimming the sea that isn't there. The Gloam got into it on the way up. It has a scar on its jaw shaped like a Dawnguard shield.
Brine Wisp
A skin of old brine, shed by the Unmoored. It swims on without it.
"Here it comes — GUARD, girl!"
"Let's see what's left in that arm."
Fennick plants his feet and draws his harpoon back. "Watch my shoulders. When they drop like this — that's your cue."
"Hff. I used to be faster. Your father was faster still."
The Ashmaw pounces!
The Ashmaw howls. The ash on the bridge pulls itself up into a smaller hound.
The Ashmaw crouches low, ash streaming off its back like smoke...
Glassback brings its whole weight down on the quarry floor!
Its glass hide clouds over and thickens.
Glassback rears up. Light splinters through its body...
The Lidless looks at you. All of it looks at you.
It blinks — it has no lid, and it blinks — and now there are more eyes.
The Lidless opens wider... and wider...
Brinefang brings the hanging sea crashing down!
SKYFALL.
Brinefang sheds a skin of brine — and the skin gets up and swims.
Brinefang climbs into the broken sky — higher — higher — and turns, and falls toward you...
Brinefang draws the upside-down sea into its throat...
Gus's Salvage & Sundries
A broken piece of Lanternfall's north cliffs. An old man, a burnt soup, two cairns.
A refugee town built from upturned boats. Six hundred people, one soup kettle.
The old strait between Lanternfall and the mainland. No water in it now — only wreckage and the long drop.

src/data/content/ch7.js.s: Ward Water
A bucket from the rationed well, for the Ember Ward.
Sunsalt Phials
The Choir's remedy for Gloam-rot. Each phial glows like a coal kept under ash.
DORAN. MAGS. LITTLE COBB. The third sunsalt team.
A rag doll with one button eye. Very brave.
Dawnmoss Seeds
Gold-green spores in a Choir apothecary tin. They will grow in anything.
Bell Clapper
The clapper of the Bellwrights' Tenor. Heavy as a promise, dented from the fall.
Three letters from Petra's bag, posted the day before the world ended.
A Letter for Wren
"My dear restless heart — I have kept a place for you." Choir seal, broken.
Rotgnawer
Undercroft rats that ate what the rot left behind, and caught it. Their bite carries it on.
Rot Bloom
Gloam-rot, given time and darkness and nothing else to do, learns to flower.
Drowned Acolyte
An acolyte of the Under-Choir. It drowned singing. It is still singing.
Knell Wisp
The last note of a bell that broke mid-toll. It drifts, still ringing, looking for the rest of itself.
Ossuary Warden
Aurenne's honored dead were buried with their swords. Some of them never put the swords down.
The Unfinished
One of Sister Mercy's Remembrances, never finished. It is trying very hard to remember a face. Any face.
Cistern Eel
They came up the drains when the sea fell into the sky. They are not going back.
Bellshell Crab
It wears a handbell for a shell. When it is angry, which is always, it rings.
Drowned Cantor
A cantor of the Under-Choir. Its voice holds the others together, the way a nail holds a coffin.
Drowned Chorister
One voice in the Drowned Choir. Alone, it is only a drowned child. Together, they are a hymn.
The Under-Choir's Precentor. He was told to hold the note until noon. He is a very obedient man.
A rust-red wyrm that nested in the Reliquary and swallowed a bell whole. It tolls when it breathes.
The Held Note breaks over you — the Dawnsong, sung backward!
The harmony falters. The Precentor's note cracks into a wail.
"Louder. LOUDER. Let the water carry it!" The cistern surges.
"Hold it... hold it until noon..."
The Precentor lifts his baton. A drowned voice answers from the water.
The choristers hold one swelling note. Silence one of them — quickly!
_BONNNG._ The sound comes out as fire.
Old Clapper thrashes. Rust and bell-metal rain from the ceiling!
Deep in Old Clapper's belly, something begins to toll. Brace yourselves!
The City of Bells, silent and drifting. Ilse's Ember Ward keeps its people breathing.

src/data/content/ch8.js.s: Brig Key
An iron key from the Vigil's captain's chair, stamped BRIG.
Vesper Orders
"Children remember the best days best. Evernoon has need of them." Signed with a weeping mask.
A patched blue kite with a painted grin, rescued from a shrike nest.
Kite-Tail Ribbon
SPD +4, evasion +6%. The tail of the first kite Pip ever built. Lucky. That's science.
Bram's Old Shield
Max HP +5%. Dented Dawnguard steel, redeemed from the Baron. Heavy as an apology.
Venn's Signet
DEF +12, RES +8, max HP +8%. Sir Aldous Venn's ring, left behind when the armor emptied. "Good lad."
Gale Shrike
They nest under the shards and steal anything shiny, blue, or belonging to Wick.
Shard Crawler
It lives upside-down on the underside of the world and does not understand why you are falling over.
Salvage that wandered off on its own. Its belly is full of airship cogs. Nobody knows why. Gaffer Quill has theories.
Wind Eel
When the sea fell into the sky, some of the eels decided the sky was just more sea.
Vesper Raider
A Vesper soldier. Living, for now. He believes he is collecting the children for their own good. So did every kidnapper ever.
They sing the lullabies. They mean every word.
Hollow Squire
Armor with a dead man in it — or the memory of one. Evernoon lends them out. They remember their own swords.
Lullaby Wisp
A stray note from the Lullaby Engine, still humming. It would very much like you to lie down.
The Lullaby Engine
A music box the size of a chapel. It keeps children dreaming their best day, forever. The pins on its drum are tiny teeth.
A knight in black armor and a weeping mask, who holds his blade high in the old Venn Guard. Under the mask is a face Bram knows.
Rustjaw
A war-boar with an iron jaw bolted on. It was a gift. It has not forgiven anyone.
Cog
The left twin. Says nothing. Hits hard. Fixes Sprocket.
The right twin. Not to be confused with the Kite. The Kite is much scarier.
Iron Moll
Former Dawnguard sergeant. "Same job, better hours." Still salutes her opponents before she flattens them.
The Gale Roc
Undefeated champion of the Scrap Arena. It was a chick when the world ended. It has been growing ever since, out of spite.
The drum turns. A lullaby pours out of every pipe at once.
Gears shriek. The Engine lurches and thrashes its brass arms!
A stray note shakes loose from the pipes and drifts into the air.
The Engine's key begins to wind... _tick... tick... tick..._
The Venn Guard falls — one perfect, merciless stroke.
A crack runs down the weeping mask. "Squires. To me." Empty armor answers.
"STAND, SQUIRE. THIS IS YOUR TRIAL."
The Penitent lifts his blade high over his shoulder — the Venn Guard. Someone is about to be cut in half. Guard!
The Gale Roc folds its wings and comes down like a falling bell!
The Roc screams. Shrikes pour in from the rafters!
The Gale Roc climbs toward the arena roof...
A shanty town of kites and scrap on a windy cliff-shard. Pip's Kites keep watch.

src/data/content/ch9.js.s: Boneyard Lift Key
Mags's key to the lift down to the Boneyard. Greasy, and proud of it.
Odessa's Mining Permit
Stamped in violet ink: ADMIT BEARERS. DO NOT DIE ON MY PROPERTY.
Pilgrim's Clock
A brass carriage clock from the Benediction. It stopped at seven minutes past the end of the world.
Gambler's Ace
LCK +12, critical rate +8%. Ferro swears it isn't marked.
Mags's Goggles
SPD +4, immune to Blind. Too big. You'll grow.
Ledger Bailiff
Odessa's debt collectors. They are polite right up to the moment they are not.
Collection Hound
Trained to find anyone who owes the Ledger money. It is never bored.
Rustback Rat
Rats that learned to eat rust. Their bite turns your blood a funny color.
Hull plate, rivets and a grudge. The Foreman builds them out of whatever falls.
Cogwisp
The last spark of a dead engine, still looking for something to turn.
Wreck Crow
Collects shiny things from the wrecks. Considers your eyes shiny.
Boneyard Picker
Scrappers who went too deep and decided the wrecks belonged to them now.
Rivet Drone
A rivet gun that learned to fly. The Foreman bolts them together in a hurry.
The Foreman
Something in the Boneyard wanted to fly again, and built itself out of every ship that couldn't.
Gilded Strongbox
The Gilded Gull's strongbox. It has been hungry for a very long time.
Hollow Pilgrim
They were flying in to hear the Vespersong. They are still singing along.
Squall Harpy
Rides the Squall the way gulls rode the sea. Screams like one, too.
Rigging Spider
Spins its webs in the shrouds. Most of what it catches is lightning.
Stormjelly
A jelly of rainwater that drifts through the Squall, swallowing lightning.
Drowned Templar
The galleon's Choir guard. It still stands its watch, a year after the watch ended.
Squallmaw
A storm drake that nested in the Benediction's mainsail and fed on a year of lightning and hymns.
Cinder Mole
Burrows through rock that has gone soft with heat. Smells of toast.
Sunslag
Molten rock with a sun-ember for a heart. It does not like to be cooled.
Flare Bat
Its wings glow from inside. In the Cinderdeep, the lights that move are never lanterns.
Ember Golem
Slag that cooled in the shape of a miner. It still swings a pick.
Shard Salamander
Lives in the lava seams. Comes out to sun itself on the sun.
The Sunworm
A worm that found a piece of the broken sun and decided to live inside it.
Dawnguard Marine
The Choir's sky marines. They were the Dawnguard once. Some of them still believe it.

And-a-one, and-a-two, and-a—

And-a-one, and-a-two, and-a-one, and-a-two, and-a-one, and-a-two, and-a—

He doesn't know. He'll never know. He'll never get to tonight.

You're the Gloam! You have to catch us before the sun goes down!

Don't laugh like that. Don't— just don't.

She looked at me. She actually *looked* at me.

Some day I'll be a knight. A real one. The kind that doesn't run.

You will be. You were. You were the best one.
_(quietly)_ And you ran, once. Back for me. That's the only running you ever did.
Have you seen my Lysa? She was just here. She's wearing her festival dress — white and gold, with a ribbon.

Have you seen my— have you seen— she was just here. She was just here. She was just here.
Lovely day for it!
For *what*, friend?

Lovely day for— lovely day for— lovely day for—
Welcome to the Festival of the Long Light. Enjoy the day.
Enjoy the day. Enjoy the day. Enjoy the day.
The fountain. Its water arcs up and hangs at the top of the arc, glittering, and does not come down.
Trays of honey-buns, glazed and golden. They are warm. They have been warm for forty years.
Nobody has ever eaten one.
The Cathedral doors are painted on. There is no inside. He never went in that day.
The Grand Lantern, humming oddly in the heat. Its light is the color of honey. It will fail tonight. It never gets to.
A cherry tree in full bloom. Petals fall from it constantly, turning in the air — and never land.
The river doesn't flow. It glitters in place, every ripple exactly where it was.
The vanity. A hairbrush with long black hairs in it, and a jar of ribbons, white and gold.
Lysa's bed. Under the pillow, a list in a child's hand: THINGS TO DO WHEN I AM GROWN UP. The list is very long.
Picture books. One is open to a drawing of an animal with a glossy black coat. Under it, in careful letters: SABLE.
A shelf of paper stars, each with a wish written inside. Most of them are about fireworks.

My boy is in there. Tam. He was nine.
The Choir says when the Hierophant's work is done the gate will open, and I'll see him at the festival. I've been waiting since the spring.
Is it still spring? I've lost count. Nothing changes up here. That's the point, they say.
Eleven months I've sat here. My Marigold is inside. Forty-one years married.

I tell myself that's a comfort.

I wanted my patients to get better. "Better" means "different." It means tomorrow.

I am. That's how I know I'm still alive.
You beat the Lift-Warden? He took my slingshot once. Did you get it back? ...No? Well. Still.

Supply line

AND THE GOOD DAY SHALL NOT END.
A statue of the Hierophant, arms open, smiling. Someone has left a child's shoe at its feet. Then another. Then hundreds.
A statue of a little girl in a festival dress, holding a ribbon. There is no name on the plinth.
The pilgrims' fire. Nobody needs it for warmth up here. They keep it lit so there is something that changes.
The lift's guarded.
Clock

The foremast. A patched sail, a patched patch, and a single kite tangled in the rigging.
Corvin's chart table. Under the charts, a small painting of a woman in a Dawnguard sky-wing coat, laughing at whoever held the brush. On the back: "H.M. — don't you DARE frame this." It is framed.
Corvin's books: "Navigation for the Reluctant," "Debts and How to Outlive Them," and a much-read book of children's bedtime stories with the price still on it.
Ilse's stove. Something is simmering. It smells like home, if home were mostly onions.
Ilse's shelf: bandages rolled tight, tinctures labeled in tiny exact handwriting. One jar just says: PIP. NO.
Nell's forge, built into the ship's boiler. It runs on coal, spite and, lately, the heat of a Sun Shard on a long chain.

A small bed with a patchwork quilt. Every patch is a different shade of yellow.
A shelf of wooden animals: a gull, a cat, a lopsided horse. Carved by a twelve-year-old, badly, with enormous care.

Miss Lysa! There you are, love.

the Ringing Bell

♪ _The festival lanterns were hung in a row, / and the Keeper's two children ran laughing below._ ♪

Sister Mercy's name has been struck from the rolls. I struck it myself. My hand would not stop shaking.
Forty-one admitted. None discharged. How did none of us ever do the arithmetic?
One Crest, one life, one light. It is carved under St. Aurel's feet. We say it every dawn.
I have said it eleven thousand times. I counted. That is my Crest, I think: Counter.
St. Aurel, holding up the first Lantern. Carved beneath her feet: *ONE CREST · ONE LIFE · ONE LIGHT.*
A pillar carved with the Seven Lanterns, from Lanternfall in the west to Skyreach above the storm. Someone has rubbed Lanternfall's carving smooth with their thumb, over many years.
The Hierophant's study. The acolyte by the altar would know if you're expected.
A painting hangs on the wall beneath a white sheet. Not a speck of dust on it. Someone uncovers it often.
...It's not ours to lift.
Letters, stacked neatly on the desk. The one on top is in your own handwriting: your letter about the stars, from two winters ago.
He kept it.
An armillary sphere of brass rings. Where the little golden sun should sit at its center, there is only an empty socket.
Treatises on the Dawnsong, scored and annotated in a fine hand. One spine has been read until it broke: *On the Inversion of Hymns.*
Correspondence with the Keepers, filed by Lantern. The Lanternfall folder is very thin. On top, in Ysolde's hand, one word: NO.
Search
...No, I don't know where the bestiaries are. I've been looking for the bestiaries since spring.
Misfiled between a hymnal and a cookbook: a loose page.

"...and so the Seven Lanterns were raised along the edge of the world, that the Hearthsun might never lose its way home. Each Keeper sings her own light. The Grand Lantern of Aurenne, first and eldest, sings for the city, and for the six."
A shelf of hymnals. And one cookbook, which explains the stains.
In a locked box marked LONG NIGHT — DO NOT LEND: a single page.
"At the turning of the summer festival, the Grand Lantern failed. The Gloam came into Aurenne through the dark, as water fills a footprint. Three hundred and twelve were taken before dawn."
Restricted shelves: Lantern schematics, Keepers' confessions, and one very old, very angry letter from Lanternfall.
*A Lexicon of Crests*, with margin notes in four different hands, arguing about Gloamweaver. None of them agree on anything, except that it should not exist.
I exist.
A tuning anvil. Forty years of bells were tuned on it. There is a dent in it shaped like a word you can't quite read.
A ledger of every noon since Tolliver began. Every entry reads RANG TRUE — except seven that read FLAT — and then, today, in large shaky letters: RANG TRUE!!!
A ledger of every noon since Tolliver began. Every entry reads RANG TRUE. Except the last seven, which read FLAT. FLAT. FLAT. FLAT. FLAT. FLAT. FLAT.
A suit of Dawnguard plate on a stand, polished to a mirror. There is a notch in the breastplate, over the heart, that has never been hammered out.
A portrait: a broad, laughing knight with a ridiculous mustache, and a young woman trying very hard not to laugh with him.
Mm. Warm. So warm.
They said I'd never be cold again.
Sister Mercy says if I'm good, I can go downstairs where it's warm.
I'm being SO good.
The Sisters stay under watch until the Lord-Commander says otherwise.
They keep offering me soup. I keep saying no. It's the longest conversation I've ever had.
The almshouse ledger, in a neat round hand. ADMITTED: forty-one. DISCHARGED: none. Beside each name, a small mark like a closed eye.
Leek and barley soup. It smells wonderful. Under the wonderful, faintly, something sweet and sleepy.
Poppy-milk. Enough to make a grown man very, very agreeable. Nobody eat the soup.

src/data/maps/ch3_rooftops.js.s: Charcoal drawings on the bell tower wall: four stick-children wearing crowns. Under them, in careful letters: *THE GUTTER CORT · PIP · NELL · TUCK · WICK.* Two of the crowns have been rubbed out and drawn back in, darker.
...Don't look at that. That's private property. Of the Court.
From up here you can see the whole City of Bells: the Cathedral, the Grand Lantern, and far off to the south, the brown thread of the Pilgrim Road.
The bells will ring at noon! And at noon tomorrow! And the noon after that!
What a summer, eh? Feels like it'll never end.
Lysa! Your brother's looking for you. He's _always_ looking for you.
Hush — the Keeper's going up. Watch the gallery. It's the best part.

src/data/maps/ch3_undercroft.js.s: Search
Valve
Examine
The brickwork here bulges outward, cracked and sweating. There is a hollow sound behind it.
Bram. Would you?
With _pleasure._
I have been wanting to hit something that didn't hit back for _days._
Scratched into the brick in chalk, at about the height of an eleven-year-old: PIP WAS ERE.
...That's from last year. I was _exploring._
A child's shoe, much too small for anyone who should be down here. The laces are still tied — in a double knot.
That's Wick's. He does double knots because he can't do bows. I keep telling him. I keep _telling_ him.
A gray hooded lantern, dropped and cracked. The Sisters of Small Mercies carry ones just like it.
A sheet of music, soaked through. The notes run from right to left.
Sable reads it, and hums. The hum makes your back teeth ache.
It is the Dawnsong. Backwards.
Memorial
The names are worn almost smooth. Under every one, the same date: THE LONG NIGHT.
A family tomb: a mother, a father, and four small names in a row. Someone has left a wooden toy horse on it. It is very old.
Tucked under a guttered candle on the last tomb: a loose, water-stained page.
"...the Keeper, Aldric Lorne, was in the lamp-room when the light failed. He might have gone down to the square, where his daughter {dim|████} was. He chose the Lantern. The city lived."
The great bell of the old foundry, cracked from crown to lip. Whatever was ringing it wanted very badly to be heard.
Ring
Bars
A woman curled on a cot, humming. When you say hello, she says it back — in exactly your voice.
An old man counting on his fingers. He gets to nine and starts again. He has been doing it, he says, for a very long time. Or possibly since this morning.
This cell is empty, except for a pair of boots standing neatly side by side. The boots are still warm.
Mercy's notes, in a neat round hand:
_Subject 31: no resistance. Children rarely resist — their memories are short and sweet. The body accepts the Gloam if it is given a memory to hold. Without one, the Gloam makes only beasts._
_Day 40. Another beast. What did HE do differently? What did he give her to hold?_
"He." Who's "he"?
Her boss, maybe. Everyone's got a boss.
Sable says nothing at all.
A cot with leather straps. The straps are child-sized.
Pressed inside one of Mercy's ledgers, a page from an old chronicle, annotated in red ink.
In the margin, in fresh red ink: _Not lost. Only waiting._
The crucible. At the bottom, a residue like burnt sugar, and a smell like a summer afternoon.

src/data/maps/ch4a_desert.js.s:
THE PILGRIM ROAD — east to Saltglass.
Carry water. Carry more water than that.
Walking to Saltglass to hear the blind Keeper. They say she can name your Crest before the Lantern does.
They say she told the Hierophant something once that made him leave in the middle of the night.
I'd like to know what. I'd like to know anything, really. That's why I walk.
Ysmay's water is the last sweet water for thirty leagues. After that it's the oasis, or the town, or you drink sand.
Mind the glass flats. Folk see things out there. Then they walk toward them.
A Choir milestone: AURENNE — 40 LEAGUES. SALTGLASS — 30.
Below, older letters someone tried to chisel away: "...WHERE THE LIGHT GOES, WE GO."
Pilgrim's Arch
A pilgrims' cairn. Every stone has a name scratched on it. Some of the names are very small, like children wrote them.
Sarn says we're not thieves. We're a toll road with knives.
Skull
The ribs of a giant wyrm arch out of the sand like the frame of a ship nobody finished building.
A weathered statue of a Keeper, holding a lamp above her head. The wind has worn away her face.
There is a cup of water at her feet. It is still cool.
Water
Saltglass is east... but that smoke in the north. Someone could be hurt out there.
Lift-glass housing
The mainmast. Someone has carved a tally into it — dozens of little marks — and, at the top, a single word: STAY.
The foremast, splintered halfway up. A torn sail flaps from it like a flag of surrender. Or a very tired wave.
Cargo crates stamped with a dozen different port seals. Half of them are empty. The other half are labeled "DEFINITELY NOT CONTRABAND."

src/data/maps/ch4a_greyspine.js.s:
GREYSPINE PASS — Frosthollow, a day's climb.
WALK SOFTLY. THE SNOW LISTENS.

QUIET WAY. Do not run. Do not shout.
Do not sing, Brother Tolle.
QUIET WAY. The snow above has been waiting all winter. Do not give it a reason.
Resting my knees. They're older than the rest of me.
Gray cloaks passed me on the lower trail two days ago. Forty of them, with a big man in front who never looked at the view.
Who climbs a mountain and doesn't look at the view?
Vigil Stone
Cairn
Frozen pack
A shrine to the Keepers of Frosthollow. Pilgrims have tied strips of cloth to it — prayers, names, a child's mitten.
Frost lily

FROSTHOLLOW. Pilgrims welcome. Beds free.
The goats are not for petting. (They bite.)
Came up for the Keeper's blessing. Stayed for the soup.
There's an army camped at the foot of the mountain. Sunburst banners. Holy soldiers, I thought — but I watched them a whole evening, and they never once prayed.
Sweep, sweep. I keep sweeping the steps to the tower.
Nobody climbs them now. I sweep them anyway. Somebody should keep the way clear.
Snow, snow, snow. Sweep, sweep, sweep.
The mountain is very generous with its snow. I am very generous with my broom. We have an understanding.
Run, Halloway. It's what Keepers' children are good at.
The Bell Stair, Wren! GO!
Memorial
Bell tower
The well is frozen over. Someone has chipped a hole in the ice and left a ladle beside it, the way you'd leave a key under a mat.
Gate road's crawling with gray cloaks, sparrow. Wrong way.
The Ice Score
I keep airing the beds. Tolle would want them aired.
He wrote from Saltglass. Two pages about the children and one line about himself: "I am managing." He underlined "managing." That boy.
A guest book. Three winters back, in a big looping hand: "Sir Aldous Venn and squire. Couldn't sleep. Lovely tea."
Steps cut into the ice by hand, worn down in the middle by centuries of monks' feet. Each step has a number carved beside it. You are on step four hundred and twelve.
A little bell is carved into the wall by the Hearthstone, and under it: FOR THE ONES WHO HAD TO LEAVE IN A HURRY.
Boots on the stair behind us. There's no going back.

src/data/maps/ch4a_saltglass.js.s:
SALTGLASS — last sweet water for thirty leagues.
The Lantern is open to pilgrims from dawn until dusk.
Caravans north: ask at the yard.
Caravan Market! Everything that came across the sand and survived it.
Prices are fixed. Fixed by me. Daily. Sometimes hourly.
Caravans
Teo hasn't stopped sulking since your little friend came out of the Lantern glowing.
Thirty days until his birthday. I'm going to need a bigger sulk-bucket.
We walked from Thistledown so my Teo could be Kindled in Saltglass light. His grandfather was. And his grandfather.
Now we wait thirty days for his birthday, in a town where water costs more than wine.
We're playing Lanterns and Gloam! I'm the Gloam! RAAAH!
Rafi is ALWAYS the Gloam. He says the Gloam is the best part.
The Gloam is NOT the best part. The best part is when the sun comes back.
The children sing on the Lantern steps every morning. The Keeper sits with them.
She says it's the worst choir she's ever heard. She cried the first time.
Yrsa looks up at you and hums three notes of the morning hymn. Then she goes back to drawing a bell in the sand.
The deep well of Saltglass. The rope goes down, and down, and down.
You drop a pebble. Four heartbeats later, very faintly: _plink._
Chimes
Master Ruel's furnace. The air above it wobbles like a mirage that can't make up its mind.
The Lamp
The lamp of Saltglass burns inside a cage of saltglass panes. The light comes out of the glass in every direction at once.
Up close it hums — low, like a cat that's pleased with itself. Or a cat that isn't.
A mirror of polished saltglass. Your reflection is a half-step behind you, as if it's thinking things over.
A mirror of polished saltglass. In it, the Lantern's light looks like dawn. In the room, it looks like noon.
A cool bed, a cold supper, and a jug of real water? Sixty gold. The water alone is worth forty.
the Cool Well
The Hierophant's men used to ride through and bless the wells.
Now they ride through and _count_ them. Why would you count wells? Wells don't go anywhere.
...Unless you expect to need every one of them.
I'm writing a ballad about the Sunscar. So far it rhymes "sand" with "sand" eleven times.
Critics call it "accurate."
I used to run the salt road in four days. Now I walk to the well and back and call it a day's work.
Best days of my life, then and now. Only now's got Nim in it.
Papa came home! He was SO dirty. Mama made him take two baths.
I drew you a picture. It's you, and the big one, and the girl with black hair, and the little one with the Crest. The little one is the biggest because he asked.
A shelf of maps — salt roads, caravan wells, wind patterns — all annotated in a quick, slanted hand. "J." in every corner.
Can you— is there a way through? Please. Please, I have a daughter.
Singing pillar
Humming wall
Glass door
A spring bubbles up through a crack in the glass. The water tastes of salt and, faintly, of thunder.
An egg of saltglass as big as a barrel. Something inside is curled up, waiting for a warmer century.
Copper pots, a wagon wheel, a child's wooden horse. A whole caravan's worth of things, polished smooth by sand.

src/data/maps/ch4b_mirefen.js.s: mp,

GREYSPINE PASS — WEST.
Someone has scratched underneath, fresh: _CLOSED. SNOW._
A girl with a black bob came out here with a bucket of something foul and made us all drink it.
I can breathe. I'd kiss her, but she looked like she'd stab me.
We were walking to Mirefen for Mother Osk's blessing. Got as far as the fever.
They won't let us in the village. Can't say I blame them. Look at my hands.
_(The veins on his wrists are black, like ink in water.)_
Da's veins are going pink again. Pink! I never thought I'd be glad of pink.
The Choir men came by on a white barge, three weeks back. Da waved to them for help.
They didn't stop. They had something in a box that hummed.
Read
A statue of a woman with a lantern, up to her knees in the fen. A string of dried frogs hangs around her neck. An offering, or a joke. In Mirefen it is hard to tell.
Gaspar's punt. The pole is worn smooth as bone where his hands go.
That's the way back to the mountains.
...There's nothing back there now. Come on.

MIREFEN. Mind the gaps. Mind the water. Mind your manners.
By order of Mother Osk, Keeper of the Mirefen Light.
Business is back! Well. People are buying soap again. That's how you know a town's recovering — soap.
Buying? Selling? Coughing? Two out of three, I can help.
Benet caught an eel this morning with two heads. Both of them looked healthy, though. That's progress.
The Choir barge came the night Mother Osk took the fever. Very polite. Very white robes.
Left the next morning. The Lantern's been dark since. Funny, that.
Benet says I shouldn't say "funny." Benet says a lot of things.
Corla's telling everyone about the two-headed eel, isn't she.
It had one head. The other one was a stick. I didn't have the heart.
Don't listen to Corla. The Choir are holy folk.
Mind you, holy folk don't usually take the light with them when they leave.
Osk's sitting up and complaining about the soup. She'll outlive us all out of spite.
Here — I'm weaving her a new blanket. The old one's been in the bog. Don't ask.
Sixty years I've known Osk. She's been dying three times and refused every time.
This time she's too tired to argue. That's what frightens me.
I'm playing Keepers and Gloam! I'm the Gloam. Rarrr.
Nettie's the Keeper. She's better now. She keeps winning.
The Drownmere's due south, straight past me. Take the punt. Bring it back — it's the only one that doesn't leak.
And if you see my brother in the water... don't talk to him. He's been dead nine years.
Nobody goes into the Drownmere. Not since the light went out. Doctor's orders.
A sack of willow bark, half-boiled. Doctor Vey's handwriting on the label: _does nothing. try anyway._
A cauldron of something gray. It smells like hope, if hope had been left out overnight.
Mag Tiller's stall: eel-skin boots, reed charms, a jar labeled ROT CURE (GENUINE). The jar is empty. The label is very confident.
A rain barrel, carefully covered. Everyone in Mirefen drinks rainwater now. Nobody trusts the fen.
Nobody goes into the Drownmere. Turn around, please.
We're not leaving. Not while she's like this.
They say the Marrow girl walked into the Drownmere and walked out carrying its heart in a jar.
I'm switching to tea.
Black veins. That's how it starts. Then the cough. Then you start seeing people in the fog.
I've got the cough. Haven't seen anyone yet.
Except you lot. Are you real?
A pot of eel stew. Rusk swears there's nothing in it but eel. Rusk is not looking at you when he says it.
A shelf of books swollen fat with damp. _The Keepers of Old_, _Fen Remedies_, and a romance called _The Heron's Kiss_ with one page dog-eared to death.
The cradle
The brass cradle where Mirefen's Dawnstone should sleep. Empty. Osk has put a jar of fireflies in it, out of spite.
The brass cradle at the heart of the Lantern. Empty. The metal is still warm in the shape of something that is not there.
Jars of herbs, eel-oil, dried frogs and something labeled in Osk's cramped hand: _DO NOT. EVER. (YES, YOU, HESK.)_
A cauldron, scrubbed clean. Somebody has been making soup every day for a woman who cannot eat it.
Gather
Examine
A statue of a Keeper, half swallowed by the bog. Her lantern is full of frogspawn. The frogs, at least, seem happy.
The Sunken Shrine. Someone kept a lamp burning here for two hundred years, until the fen rose. You can still see the soot on the stones.

src/data/maps/ch4b_stormcrown.js.s: Storm-seam
A mooring post as thick as a man, scorched black on the side that faces the mountain. Lightning loves this place.
The Halcyon's mainmast. A tally of little lightning bolts is carved into it. Forty-one. The last one is very fresh, and very deep.
The Gull's Nest — highest beds in Solmere! Eighty gold. The view's free. The vertigo's also free.
the Gull's Nest
Windward Exchange! Everything up here came up on a ship, so everything up here costs a ship's worth. Have a browse.
The isle's risen a full fathom since this morning. I could feel it in my knees.
Skyreach floats on light, they say. Seems it can float on stubbornness too, in a pinch.
Skyreach floats on the Lantern's light, child. Has done for three hundred years.
And the light holds the Thunderhead down beneath us. Two jobs, one Lantern. That's the old story.
The Ardent says it's just a story. The Ardent gave our stone away. I'm old. I notice things.
You went down beneath the isle for us. Even though you think the Hierophant is wrong.
I don't know what to do with that. I have been praying about it. The wind has not answered.
When the Vespersong is sung, no one will ever be lost to the storm again. No more empty chairs at supper.
Don't you want that? Doesn't everyone want that?
Ilka's put Skyreach-cut lift-crystals in that old tub. She'll climb like a lark now.
Your captain flew her up through the Stormcrown on _desert glass_. Nobody up here will ever buy him a drink again — they'll be too busy telling the story.
I saw you come up through the storm. Thought you were a falling barn.
Then I thought: no, a barn would fly better.
The Lord-Commander came on a black warship, three weeks back. The Ardent handed him our stone on the steps of the Lantern, and everybody cheered.
I cheered. Loudest of anyone.
...I don't know why I cheered.
Depart
A fountain fed by rain-catchers. Coins glint at the bottom: offerings to the wind, for safe flights. There are a great many coins.
The Halcyon, nose-down in what used to be Ilka's shed. One mast is broken. The other is somehow holding a chicken.
Ilka's yard. Where the Halcyon crashed, there is a neat pile of salvaged timber labeled, in large letters, CORVIN'S. YOU'RE PAYING FOR THIS.
The Keel Lift's for the Keel-crew only. Ardent's orders.
The cradle
In the brass cradle where Skyreach's Dawnstone should sit, a single silver tuning fork stands upright, humming to itself.
You know that note. You have been carrying it in your pack for weeks.

src/data/maps/ch4b_verdance.js.s:
THE THORNWOOD.
Keeper's grove beyond. Walk softly; the trees are listening.
_(Underneath, newer, in charcoal: CLOSED. THORNS. DO NOT.)_
Forage, fletching, and things that fix you. Mostly the first two. Have a look.
The Hollow Log. Hollow log, soft moss, warm stew. Seventy gold, and I'll even let you choose which log.
the Hollow Log
The soldiers came a month back. Fifty of them, white and gold, the Hierophant's sun on every shield.
The big one with the beard didn't even go in. Sat on my woodpile eating our apples while his men carried the Keeper's light out in a box.
Didn't pay for the apples, either.
You've seen her? Truly? Is she— is she very old?
Of course she is. I only meant — is she very _kind_? I always imagined she was.
I'm writing an epic about Keeper Elowen. Nobody in Rootholm has seen her in thirty years.
Some say she is four hundred years old. Some say she has turned into a tree. I have rhymed both possibilities, just in case.
I'm not allowed in the Tangle anymore. Or near the Tangle. Or near anyone who's been near the Tangle.
Mum's very thorough.
I tied a ribbon for Gran on the Memory Tree. A yellow one. She liked yellow.
The pretty lights in the forest weren't her. Ilse said. Ilse says it's all right to miss her anyway.
When I'm sixteen I'm going to be a Warden like the big one. Or a Rogue like the small one.
He said I could be both. He said that's allowed now. Is that allowed now?
The Memory Tree
Fern's crates: bundles of arrows fletched with jay feathers, jars of honey, a sign reading NO HAGGLING, and under it, smaller: (a little haggling).
